label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa contra gentiles I.42: A divine nature individuated through another entails…
interpretation: These are the source’s individuation alternatives and excluded multiplication modes. Their application presupposes the divine nature and its no-addition/nonmaterial conditions. They are not independently established for arbitrary whole essences or a selected underived root, and no afterwards-all-others-receive-esse premise is imported to prove this prior uniqueness. Based on the verified complete Pegis translation chapter; no pinned Latin reading or formal proof/premise truth is asserted.
